tasks.title: Lifetime labels: longest and pairs
tasks.statement: longest<'a>(a, b) → &'a str — the longer one by number of characters (the first on a tie). first_two<'a>(s) → (&'a str, &'a str) — the first two words of the string (an empty string in place of a missing one). shorter_of<'a>(words: &[&'a str]) → Option<&'a str> — the shortest word (the first on a tie).
tasks.hint: The label 'a on all references says: the result lives no longer than both arguments; in shorter_of the words carry 'a inside the slice.

tasks.title: Two independent labels
tasks.statement: pick_first<'a, 'b>(a: &'a str, _b: &'b str) → &'a str always returns a. In the driver the second string dies before the result — this is allowed only with TWO labels. Also implement between<'a, 'b>(text: &'a str, left: &'b str, right: &'b str) → Option<&'a str> — the part of text between the first left and the next right.
tasks.hint: Give each reference its own label: the result is tied only to 'a, and 'b may end earlier.

tasks.title: Slices without copying: key=value
tasks.statement: split_kv<'a>(line: &'a str) → Option<(&'a str, &'a str)> — a key=value line: the key and the value with no spaces at the edges; None if there is no "=" or the key is empty. parse_lines<'a>(text: &'a str) → Vec<(&'a str, &'a str)> — all valid lines. The result is slices of the original text, no copies.
tasks.hint: trim() returns a slice of the same string — no copies are made; filter_map(split_kv) works because split_kv takes &str.

tasks.title: Iterator of slices: Tokens<'a>
tasks.statement: Tokens<'a> keeps the rest of the text and yields words (runs of non-whitespace) as &'a str — without copying. Implement Tokens::new(text) and Iterator<Item = &'a str>. The words must be slices of the original string (the same buffer).
tasks.hint: split_at(end) splits a slice into a word and the rest — both with the same lifetime 'a.

tasks.title: Fix it: the iterator captures a reference
tasks.statement: evens_of returns an iterator over the even numbers of a vector, but the compiler complains: the hidden type captures a lifetime that is not in the bounds. Add a label to the signature that ties the iterator to the argument.
tasks.hint: + '_ means: the iterator lives no longer than the borrowed argument.

tasks.title: 'static: tables and constants
tasks.statement: static NAMES: [&str; 4] = ["north", "east", "south", "west"]. direction_name(i: usize) → &'static str (the index wraps around), direction_index(name: &str) → Option<usize>, turn(from: &str, steps: i32) → Option<&'static str> — turn by steps quarters (may be negative). const QUARTER: i32 = 90.
tasks.hint: rem_euclid(4) gives a non-negative remainder even for negative turns.

tasks.title: A list on Box: length, sum, reversal
tasks.statement: List { Cons(i32, Box<List>), Nil }. len(&List), sum(&List), to_vec(&List), reverse(List) → List (takes the list and rearranges the links, with no new allocations through clone), from_slice(&[i32]) → List.
tasks.hint: A right-to-left fold (rev()) builds a list with the head first; reverse moves each link into a new list.

tasks.title: A binary search tree on Box
tasks.statement: Tree { root: Option<Box<Node>> } with methods insert(&mut self, k) (duplicates are ignored), contains(&self, k) → bool, height(&self) → usize (empty is 0), in_order(&self) → Vec<i32>, min(&self) → Option<i32>.
tasks.hint: In insert walk down through &mut Option<Box<Node>>: while it is Some, pick a side, and on None store the new node.

tasks.title: States through Box<dyn State>
tasks.statement: Trait State: name(&self) → &'static str and next(self: Box<Self>, event: &str) → Box<dyn State>. Implement Idle → ("start") Running → ("pause") Paused → ("resume") Running; from Running on "stop" → Idle; Paused on "stop" → Idle; an unknown event keeps the state. run(events: &[&str]) → Vec<&'static str> — the state names after each event.
tasks.hint: self: Box<Self> lets you take and return yourself (_ => self) or replace it with another state.

tasks.title: Pointer sizes and Box
tasks.statement: sizes() → [usize; 8]: size_of for &u8, Box<u8>, Box<[u8; 100]>, &[u8], Box<dyn Fn()>, Option<Box<u8>>, Option<&u8>, Rc<[u8; 100]> — in that order. Which of them are one word, and which are two?
tasks.hint: A slice and dyn carry an extra word; an array of known length is an ordinary pointer; Option over a pointer is no bigger than the pointer.

tasks.title: Your own smart pointer: Deref
tasks.statement: MyBox<T>(T) with new(x). Implement Deref (Target = T) and DerefMut. After that hello(&MyBox<String>) accepts &str thanks to deref coercion, and *b gives the inner value. shout(b: &MyBox<String>) → String calls a string method directly.
tasks.hint: deref returns &self.0; DerefMut returns &mut self.0. The coercion &MyBox<String> → &String → &str is done by the compiler.

tasks.title: Deref to a slice: Sorted
tasks.statement: Sorted keeps a Vec<i32> in sorted order. new(v) sorts; insert(&mut self, x) inserts at the right place (binary search); Deref<Target = [i32]> gives len(), iter(), first(), contains() and slices without repeating the methods.
tasks.hint: Target = [i32], deref returns &self.0 — the vector turns into a slice automatically.

tasks.title: Drop order: a log
tasks.statement: Guard(name, log) appends "drop name" to a shared log when destroyed. Implement Drop. scenario(log) creates Guards a, b, c in one block, then a nested block with d, then explicitly drop(b), and finally returns the log. Check the order: variables die in the reverse order of declaration.
tasks.hint: The log is shared: Rc<RefCell<Vec<String>>>; in drop we write with log.borrow_mut().push(...).

tasks.title: drop, forget and moves
tasks.statement: Guard(&'static str) prints "drop <name>" when destroyed, consume(g) prints "consume". Write trace(): create Guards a, b, c; pass b to consume (the Guard dies inside); then print "mid"; give c to std::mem::forget (the destructor is not called); print "end". What happens to a?
tasks.hint: consume(b) takes b: drop b fires at the exit of consume; forget(c) does not run drop; a dies at the closing brace.

tasks.title: RAII: a transaction rolls back by itself
tasks.statement: Tx<'a> borrows &'a mut Vec<i32> (the "database"). begin(db) remembers the original size; push(&mut self, x) adds a number; commit(self) makes it permanent; if Tx is destroyed without commit, Drop rolls the database back to the original length. This way the "changes" do not leak out on an error or an early exit.
tasks.hint: commit(mut self) sets a flag and the Tx itself dies on exit: Drop sees committed = true and rolls nothing back.

tasks.title: Rc: watching the counter
tasks.statement: counts() → Vec<usize>: create an Rc<String>, record strong_count; clone it twice — record again; in a nested block make one more clone and record it; after the block and after dropping one clone — record. Six numbers in total.
tasks.hint: strong_count after each action: 1, 3, 4, 3, 2, 1 — a clone increases it, leaving the block and drop decrease it.

tasks.title: Rc<RefCell<Account>>: a shared account
tasks.statement: Account { balance: i64 }. Two owners share one account through Rc<RefCell<Account>>. deposit(acc, n) and withdraw(acc, n) → Result<(), String> with the error «insufficient funds: needed N, present M»; transfer(from, to, n) → Result<(), String> transfers between two accounts (if from and to are the same account, the transfer changes nothing).
tasks.hint: If from and to are the same account, a second borrow_mut would panic: check Rc::ptr_eq beforehand.

tasks.title: Shared nodes: Rc in a graph without cycles
tasks.statement: Node { val: i32, kids: Vec<Rc<Node>> }. total(&Node) → i32 — the sum over all paths (a shared node is counted every time), unique_total(&Node) → i32 — each node once (a set of *const Node addresses). refs(&Rc<Node>) → usize — strong_count.
tasks.hint: A node's address is n as *const Node; the seen set keeps a shared node from being visited twice.

tasks.title: RefCell: try_borrow without panics
tasks.statement: probe() → Vec<bool>: create a RefCell<i32>; record the is_ok() results of this sequence: try_borrow_mut() on a free cell; try_borrow() while a mutable borrow is alive; try_borrow_mut() while a shared borrow is alive; try_borrow() with two shared borrows; try_borrow_mut() after everything is released.
tasks.hint: A live Ref or RefMut is a variable in scope; { … } blocks release the borrow.

tasks.title: Cell: a counter through &self
tasks.statement: Stats keeps hits: Cell<u32> and last: Cell<Option<i32>>. touch(&self, x) increases hits and remembers x in last; hits() and last() return the values. All methods take &self — mutation inside a shared reference (interior mutability without RefCell).
tasks.hint: Cell::get/set work with copyable values without handing out references — so they need no run-time checks.

tasks.title: Observers on Weak
tasks.statement: Subject keeps a Vec<Weak<RefCell<Vec<String>>>> — the observers' "mailboxes". subscribe(&mut self, inbox: &Rc<RefCell<Vec<String>>>) adds a weak reference; publish(&mut self, msg) → usize puts the message into the live mailboxes, removes the dead ones and returns the number delivered.
tasks.hint: Rc::downgrade(&rc) is a weak reference; upgrade() returns None when no owners are left.

tasks.title: A tree with Weak to the parent
tasks.statement: Node { name: String, parent: RefCell<Weak<Node>>, kids: RefCell<Vec<Rc<Node>>> }. new(name) → Rc<Node>; add_child(parent: &Rc<Node>, child: Rc<Node>) attaches a child and stores a weak reference to the parent; path(n: &Rc<Node>) → String — the path from the root, "a/b/c".
tasks.hint: The parent holds its children strongly (kids), and the child holds the parent weakly (parent), so there is no cycle and after drop(root) the root is freed.

tasks.title: An Rc cycle: the leak and its fix
tasks.statement: cycle_counts() → Vec<usize>: create two nodes Node { next: RefCell<Option<Rc<Node>>> }; record the strong_count of both; link them to each other and record again; break the cycle (take()) and record once more. Six numbers in total: a, b before; a, b in the cycle; a, b after.
tasks.hint: While the cycle is closed, each node has count 2 — after leaving the function they would never be freed; take() breaks the link.

tasks.title: Arc: counter, try_unwrap and make_mut
tasks.statement: arc_demo() → (usize, bool, Vec<i32>, Vec<i32>): create an Arc<Vec<i32>> from [1, 2, 3]; clone it; record strong_count; attempt Arc::try_unwrap with two owners (is_err); then through Arc::make_mut on the clone append 4 (a copy, because there are two owners) — return the original and the modified clone.
tasks.hint: try_unwrap returns Err while there are other owners; make_mut clones the data if the Arc is not unique.

tasks.title: Cow: copy only when necessary
tasks.statement: normalize(s: &str) → Cow<str>: if the string has tabs or consecutive spaces, return a fixed copy (tabs → space, runs of spaces → one); otherwise return Cow::Borrowed with no copy. is_borrowed(c) → bool — whether the Cow is borrowed.
tasks.hint: In the branch with no changes return Cow::Borrowed(s) — the same address, no copy.

tasks.title: mem::replace, take and swap
tasks.statement: Machine { state: State, items: Vec<String>, name: String }. finish(&mut self) → State — switch the state to Done and return the previous one (mem::replace); drain_items(&mut self) → Vec<String> — take all the items (mem::take); swap_name(&mut self, other: &mut Machine) — swap the names (mem::swap).
tasks.hint: mem::replace(&mut field, new) returns the old value; mem::take puts in the Default (an empty Vec).

tasks.title: String interning: Rc<str>
tasks.statement: Interner keeps a HashMap<String, Rc<str>>. intern(&mut self, s: &str) → Rc<str> returns the same Rc for equal strings (memory is allocated once); len(&self) → usize — the number of distinct strings; total_refs(&self) → usize — the sum of strong_count over all entries.
tasks.hint: Rc<str> is a fat pointer (address and length); Rc::from(&str) copies the bytes once into a block with the counters.

tasks.title: A tree in an arena: indexes instead of pointers
tasks.statement: Arena { nodes: Vec<Item> } with Item { name, parent: Option<usize>, kids: Vec<usize> }. add(name, parent: Option<usize>) → usize — the id of the new node (and an entry in the parent's kids); depth(id) → usize — the number of ancestors; path(id) → String, "a/b/c"; leaves(&self) → Vec<&str> — names of nodes with no children in id order. No Rc, no RefCell.
tasks.hint: Links are indexes into one Vec: when adding a node, append its id to the parent's kids.

tasks.title: An immutable list with a shared tail
tasks.statement: type Link = Option<Rc<Node>>; Node { val, next: Link }. push(list: &Link, v) → Link creates a new head that shares the tail with the old list; to_vec(&Link); len(&Link); tail_refs(list: &Link) → usize — the head's strong_count (how many lists share this tail).
tasks.hint: list.clone() on an Option<Rc<…>> copies only the pointer and increases the counter: the tail is shared.

tasks.title: A doubly linked list: Rc forward, Weak backward
tasks.statement: DList { head: Option<Rc<RefCell<DNode>>>, tail: Option<Rc<RefCell<DNode>>> } with DNode { val, next: Option<Rc<RefCell<DNode>>>, prev: Option<Weak<RefCell<DNode>>> }. push_back(v); push_front(v); pop_back() → Option<i32>; forward() → Vec<i32> (along next); backward() → Vec<i32> (along prev from the tail).
tasks.hint: Forward (next) are strong Rc, backward (prev) are Weak; in pop_back do not forget to clear next on the new tail.
